bull_bear.body:
- Operator status in its key assets, which the Company states enables greater control over field development planning, capital allocation and execution of production enhancement programmes
- Diversified producing and exploration asset base across nine contract areas in five hydrocarbon basins following the Composite Scheme of Arrangement
- Among the few companies in India leveraging Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for subsurface imaging and optimal well placement; integrated ML of wireline log and seismic data has identified sweet spots and field extensions with high drilling success rates
- Pioneer in India in adopting cloud-based platforms for subsurface data management; pad-based drilling with 24x7 real-time data monitoring to reduce non-productive time
- Advanced hydraulic fracturing capability — geomechanics-optimised frac design and real-time proppant placement contributed to a substantial production increase at Bakrol, and re-fracturing of previously stimulated wells delivered a multi-fold increase in production
- Development capital expenditure funded entirely through internal cash accruals, without debt funding
- IND A/Stable long-term and IND A1 short-term credit ratings from India Ratings & Research
- Experienced technical team and a disciplined capital allocation framework with a strong balance sheet (management's stated positioning)
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Commodity price risk — Revenues are directly influenced by international crude oil prices and Government-notified domestic natural gas prices, which are inherently volatile and driven by global supply-demand dynamics, geopolitical developments, OPEC+ production policies, currency fluctuations and macroeconomic conditions. Adverse price movements hit revenue, profitability and investment returns.
- Customer concentration risk — Indian Oil Corporation Limited is the anchor buyer of a majority of the crude oil produced; any adverse change in IOCL's purchasing pattern, pricing terms or offtake volumes could materially impact revenue and operations. Mitigated only partly by selling select volumes to private refineries.
- Resource and reservoir risk — The business depends on successful discovery, development and commercial recovery of hydrocarbon reserves. Reserve estimates rest on geological, geophysical and engineering interpretations that carry inherent uncertainty, so variations in reservoir performance or recovery factors can change future production and financial performance.
- Mature-field decline and production sustainability — Mature field operations face declining reservoir pressure, water handling and enhanced recovery requirements; sustaining production from ageing assets demands continuous investment in reservoir studies, workovers, artificial lift and other production enhancement technologies.
- Infrastructure and evacuation constraints — Access to pipelines, evacuation facilities, processing infrastructure and storage capacity may limit commercialisation of hydrocarbon production in certain operating areas — management's FY'27 plan makes bringing evacuation capacity online the critical enabler of ramp-up at Bakrol, Karjisan and Cambay, and names evacuation constraints as the focus at Dangeru.
- Operational and project execution risk — Technically complex drilling, production and field development work exposes the Company to project delays, equipment failures, contractor performance, infrastructure constraints and unforeseen subsurface conditions, any of which can hit production targets and project economics.
- Regulatory, approval and compliance risk — The upstream sector requires multiple statutory approvals and environmental clearances; changes in regulatory requirements or delays in approvals affect operations and development timelines. The secretarial auditor also reported one compliance lapse for FY26 — E-Form MGT-14 for the April 08, 2025 Board resolution on availment of a bank guarantee from Kotak Mahindra Bank for the Cambay, Bakrol, Lohar and Karjisan fields was filed belatedly.
- Health, safety and environmental (HSE) risk — Oil and gas operations carry inherent HSE risks; failure to manage them could cause operational disruptions, environmental incidents, reputational damage and financial liabilities. Mitigated through HSE policies, training, emergency preparedness, safety audits and insurance cover on operated assets.
- Stakeholder and community relations risk — Operations sit in areas where relationships with local communities and landowners are essential; social or community issues, including land access pressure from increasing urbanisation around operating areas, may affect project execution and operational continuity.
- Climate change and energy-transition risk — The global shift towards lower-carbon energy, evolving climate-related regulations and rising stakeholder expectations on environmental performance may reshape the long-term operating environment for upstream oil and gas, and compliance may require additional operational and capital expenditure.
- Technology and cybersecurity risk — Growing reliance on digital technologies, operational systems and information infrastructure exposes the Company to cybersecurity threats, data security risks and potential business disruption.

business.body: The Company operates in a single business segment of Oil and Gas Exploration and Production (E&P), encompassing the exploration, development and production of crude oil and natural gas. Its producing asset portfolio comprises the Bakrol, Lohar, Karjisan and Cambay fields located in Gujarat, along with interests in exploration assets across multiple hydrocarbon basins; the Dangeru Contract Area commenced production during FY2025-26 and development activities progressed at Duarmara in the Assam onshore basin. Crude oil is marketed to domestic refiners, with Indian Oil Corporation Limited as the anchor buyer, while natural gas is sold to industrial consumers in the vicinity of the operating fields.

outlook.body:
- Six strategic pillars: Production Optimization, Resource to Reserve, People & Culture, Technology & Innovation, Sustainability, and HSSE & Governance
- Production optimization — maximise value from existing assets through enhanced reservoir management and recovery, optimised well performance and uptime, technology and data analytics, and cost efficiency across operations
- Resource to reserve — convert resources into reserves via appraisal and exploration, efficient development of discovered resources, focus on long-life high-value projects, stronger subsurface capabilities and a healthy reserve replacement ratio
- Data-led, de-risked development: establish technical and commercial confidence through initial drilling, then use those results to allocate capital progressively towards opportunities with demonstrated potential
- Translate the FY'26 development pipeline into sustained production growth in FY'27 — a deliberate progression from de-risking to development, production ramp-up and value creation
- Bring the required evacuation capacity online as the critical enabler of production ramp-up across Bakrol, Karjisan and Cambay
- Fund growth through internal cash accruals without debt funding, maintaining a strong balance sheet and disciplined capital allocation
- Realise merger synergies — integrate people, processes and systems into a unified operating model for technical collaboration, cost optimisation and improved execution efficiency
- Sustain production from core producing fields while bringing newer fields into production through timely development, towards building a resilient, diversified, mid-sized energy company (Future Plan of Action)
- Long-term objective: build a leading independent upstream energy company in India through operational excellence, responsible growth and disciplined execution
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: FY 2025-26 was an execution year in which the Company deployed development capital across its expanded asset portfolio, funded primarily through internal accruals. It progressed drilling activities across Karjisan, Bakrol, Cambay, Dangeru and Duarmara: four wells were drilled at Karjisan (where production approximately doubled during the year), two at Bakrol as the first phase of a newly launched 10-well drilling campaign, and one at Cambay under the already approved three-well field development plan. The Dangeru Contract Area commenced production towards the end of July 2025 following receipt of its Petroleum Mining Lease in February 2025, and drilling was initiated at Duarmara, marking the Company's foray into the Assam onshore basin. Multiple FDP approvals advanced during the year, which management says gives visibility on the next phase of drilling. For FY'27 the Company plans to drill the remaining eight wells of the approved 10-well FDP at Bakrol, a seven-well programme at Karjisan across newly opened fault blocks, and the remaining wells committed under the Cambay FDP subject to Joint Venture partner approvals; alongside drilling, bringing the required evacuation capacity online is described as critical to enabling the ramp-up across Bakrol, Karjisan and Cambay. At Dangeru the focus is on resolving evacuation constraints and frac-led ramp-up, and at Duarmara on re-perforation, establishing oil commerciality and progressing towards production. Infrastructure development and debottlenecking across the portfolio continue. On the sustainability side, a 100 KW on-site solar power plant was installed and commissioned at Karjisan Field (investment of approx. Rs 36 lacs), integrated with the State Electricity Grid, and capital investment on energy conservation equipment was Rs. 80,28,819.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's GDP grew by approximately 7.7% during FY 2025-26, supported by strong domestic consumption, sustained public capital expenditure and infrastructure development
- Brent crude traded within a range of approximately US$ 60-82 per barrel during FY 2025-26; despite short-term fluctuations, crude prices largely remained supportive for upstream producers
- India's domestic consumption of petroleum products increased to approximately 241.61 million metric tonnes (MMT), while domestic crude oil production remained relatively stable at approximately 27.95 MMT
- Natural gas is strengthening its position in India's energy mix; LNG imports and total gas consumption grew, aided by demand from City Gas Distribution, fertiliser, power and industrial sectors and expanding pipeline infrastructure — a significant opportunity for domestic gas producers
- Government policy support — HELP, OALP and ease-of-doing-business measures — is expected to facilitate faster monetisation of discovered resources and improve the sector's investment attractiveness
- The Oilfields (Regulation and Development) Amendment Act, 2025 introduces the concept of a petroleum lease, more stable lease terms, infrastructure sharing and stronger dispute resolution, which management views as supportive of long-term sector development
- Rising urbanisation, industrial activity, transportation demand and per capita energy consumption are expected to drive sustained growth in oil and natural gas requirements over coming decades
- Revenue realisation remains linked to prevailing international crude oil benchmarks and Government-notified domestic natural gas prices
- The Company's expanded asset portfolio following the Scheme of Arrangement offers operational synergies, infrastructure optimisation, improved reservoir management and enhanced recovery initiatives
- Threats to the outlook: commodity price volatility, regulatory and approval complexity, declining reservoir pressure and water handling in mature fields, infrastructure and evacuation constraints, stricter environmental/HSE expectations, and land access/community issues from urbanisation around operating areas
- Structural demand outlook for hydrocarbons in India remains robust notwithstanding commodity price volatility and geopolitical developments

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Antelopus Selan Energy Limited (formerly Selan Exploration Technology Limited) is an independent Indian upstream oil and gas company with interests in nine contract areas across five hydrocarbon basins.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company operates in a single business segment of Oil and Gas Exploration and Production (E&P), encompassing the exploration, development and production of crude oil and natural gas. Its producing asset portfolio comprises the Bakrol, Lohar, Karjisan and Cambay fields located in Gujarat, along with interests in exploration assets across multiple hydrocarbon basins; the Dangeru Contract Area commenced production during FY2025-26 and development activities progressed at Duarmara in the Assam onshore basin. Crude oil is marketed to domestic refiners, with Indian Oil Corporation Limited as the anchor buyer, while natural gas is sold to industrial consumers in the vicinity of the operating fields.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body: - Antelopus Energy Private Limited — related party: Transferor Company under the Composite Scheme of Arrangement approved by NCLT Chandigarh Bench on June 10, 2025 (rectified July 01, 2025); the Scheme became effective July 05, 2025 and the Company allotted 1,99,62,358 equity shares of face value INR 10 each to its shareholders. Not a subsidiary, JV or associate as at March 31, 2026.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body: - **Oil and Gas Exploration and Production (E&P):** Crude oil, Natural gas

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Domestic refiners (India) — Indian Oil Corporation Limited as anchor buyer, with select volumes to private refineries
- Industrial consumers of natural gas in the vicinity of the Company's operating fields
- India — upstream oil and gas; operating fields in Gujarat and the Assam onshore basin

certifications.title: Certs (RHP)
certifications.body: ISO 14001:2015 Environmental Management System Certification (received during FY'26)

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's GDP grew by approximately 7.7% during FY 2025-26, supported by strong domestic consumption, sustained public capital expenditure and infrastructure development
- Brent crude traded within a range of approximately US$ 60-82 per barrel during FY 2025-26; despite short-term fluctuations, crude prices largely remained supportive for upstream producers
- India's domestic consumption of petroleum products increased to approximately 241.61 million metric tonnes (MMT), while domestic crude oil production remained relatively stable at approximately 27.95 MMT
- Natural gas is strengthening its position in India's energy mix; LNG imports and total gas consumption grew, aided by demand from City Gas Distribution, fertiliser, power and industrial sectors and expanding pipeline infrastructure — a significant opportunity for domestic gas producers
- Government policy support — HELP, OALP and ease-of-doing-business measures — is expected to facilitate faster monetisation of discovered resources and improve the sector's investment attractiveness
- The Oilfields (Regulation and Development) Amendment Act, 2025 introduces the concept of a petroleum lease, more stable lease terms, infrastructure sharing and stronger dispute resolution, which management views as supportive of long-term sector development
- Rising urbanisation, industrial activity, transportation demand and per capita energy consumption are expected to drive sustained growth in oil and natural gas requirements over coming decades
- Revenue realisation remains linked to prevailing international crude oil benchmarks and Government-notified domestic natural gas prices
- The Company's expanded asset portfolio following the Scheme of Arrangement offers operational synergies, infrastructure optimisation, improved reservoir management and enhanced recovery initiatives
- Threats to the outlook: commodity price volatility, regulatory and approval complexity, declining reservoir pressure and water handling in mature fields, infrastructure and evacuation constraints, stricter environmental/HSE expectations, and land access/community issues from urbanisation around operating areas
- Structural demand outlook for hydrocarbons in India remains robust notwithstanding commodity price volatility and geopolitical developments

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Six strategic pillars: Production Optimization, Resource to Reserve, People & Culture, Technology & Innovation, Sustainability, and HSSE & Governance
- Production optimization — maximise value from existing assets through enhanced reservoir management and recovery, optimised well performance and uptime, technology and data analytics, and cost efficiency across operations
- Resource to reserve — convert resources into reserves via appraisal and exploration, efficient development of discovered resources, focus on long-life high-value projects, stronger subsurface capabilities and a healthy reserve replacement ratio
- Data-led, de-risked development: establish technical and commercial confidence through initial drilling, then use those results to allocate capital progressively towards opportunities with demonstrated potential
- Translate the FY'26 development pipeline into sustained production growth in FY'27 — a deliberate progression from de-risking to development, production ramp-up and value creation
- Bring the required evacuation capacity online as the critical enabler of production ramp-up across Bakrol, Karjisan and Cambay
- Fund growth through internal cash accruals without debt funding, maintaining a strong balance sheet and disciplined capital allocation
- Realise merger synergies — integrate people, processes and systems into a unified operating model for technical collaboration, cost optimisation and improved execution efficiency
- Sustain production from core producing fields while bringing newer fields into production through timely development, towards building a resilient, diversified, mid-sized energy company (Future Plan of Action)
- Long-term objective: build a leading independent upstream energy company in India through operational excellence, responsible growth and disciplined execution

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: FY 2025-26 was an execution year in which the Company deployed development capital across its expanded asset portfolio, funded primarily through internal accruals. It progressed drilling activities across Karjisan, Bakrol, Cambay, Dangeru and Duarmara: four wells were drilled at Karjisan (where production approximately doubled during the year), two at Bakrol as the first phase of a newly launched 10-well drilling campaign, and one at Cambay under the already approved three-well field development plan. The Dangeru Contract Area commenced production towards the end of July 2025 following receipt of its Petroleum Mining Lease in February 2025, and drilling was initiated at Duarmara, marking the Company's foray into the Assam onshore basin. Multiple FDP approvals advanced during the year, which management says gives visibility on the next phase of drilling. For FY'27 the Company plans to drill the remaining eight wells of the approved 10-well FDP at Bakrol, a seven-well programme at Karjisan across newly opened fault blocks, and the remaining wells committed under the Cambay FDP subject to Joint Venture partner approvals; alongside drilling, bringing the required evacuation capacity online is described as critical to enabling the ramp-up across Bakrol, Karjisan and Cambay. At Dangeru the focus is on resolving evacuation constraints and frac-led ramp-up, and at Duarmara on re-perforation, establishing oil commerciality and progressing towards production. Infrastructure development and debottlenecking across the portfolio continue. On the sustainability side, a 100 KW on-site solar power plant was installed and commissioned at Karjisan Field (investment of approx. Rs 36 lacs), integrated with the State Electricity Grid, and capital investment on energy conservation equipment was Rs. 80,28,819.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Operator status in its key assets, which the Company states enables greater control over field development planning, capital allocation and execution of production enhancement programmes
- Diversified producing and exploration asset base across nine contract areas in five hydrocarbon basins following the Composite Scheme of Arrangement
- Among the few companies in India leveraging Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for subsurface imaging and optimal well placement; integrated ML of wireline log and seismic data has identified sweet spots and field extensions with high drilling success rates
- Pioneer in India in adopting cloud-based platforms for subsurface data management; pad-based drilling with 24x7 real-time data monitoring to reduce non-productive time
- Advanced hydraulic fracturing capability — geomechanics-optimised frac design and real-time proppant placement contributed to a substantial production increase at Bakrol, and re-fracturing of previously stimulated wells delivered a multi-fold increase in production
- Development capital expenditure funded entirely through internal cash accruals, without debt funding
- IND A/Stable long-term and IND A1 short-term credit ratings from India Ratings & Research
- Experienced technical team and a disciplined capital allocation framework with a strong balance sheet (management's stated positioning)

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Commodity price risk — Revenues are directly influenced by international crude oil prices and Government-notified domestic natural gas prices, which are inherently volatile and driven by global supply-demand dynamics, geopolitical developments, OPEC+ production policies, currency fluctuations and macroeconomic conditions. Adverse price movements hit revenue, profitability and investment returns.
- Customer concentration risk — Indian Oil Corporation Limited is the anchor buyer of a majority of the crude oil produced; any adverse change in IOCL's purchasing pattern, pricing terms or offtake volumes could materially impact revenue and operations. Mitigated only partly by selling select volumes to private refineries.
- Resource and reservoir risk — The business depends on successful discovery, development and commercial recovery of hydrocarbon reserves. Reserve estimates rest on geological, geophysical and engineering interpretations that carry inherent uncertainty, so variations in reservoir performance or recovery factors can change future production and financial performance.
- Mature-field decline and production sustainability — Mature field operations face declining reservoir pressure, water handling and enhanced recovery requirements; sustaining production from ageing assets demands continuous investment in reservoir studies, workovers, artificial lift and other production enhancement technologies.
- Infrastructure and evacuation constraints — Access to pipelines, evacuation facilities, processing infrastructure and storage capacity may limit commercialisation of hydrocarbon production in certain operating areas — management's FY'27 plan makes bringing evacuation capacity online the critical enabler of ramp-up at Bakrol, Karjisan and Cambay, and names evacuation constraints as the focus at Dangeru.
- Operational and project execution risk — Technically complex drilling, production and field development work exposes the Company to project delays, equipment failures, contractor performance, infrastructure constraints and unforeseen subsurface conditions, any of which can hit production targets and project economics.
- Regulatory, approval and compliance risk — The upstream sector requires multiple statutory approvals and environmental clearances; changes in regulatory requirements or delays in approvals affect operations and development timelines. The secretarial auditor also reported one compliance lapse for FY26 — E-Form MGT-14 for the April 08, 2025 Board resolution on availment of a bank guarantee from Kotak Mahindra Bank for the Cambay, Bakrol, Lohar and Karjisan fields was filed belatedly.
- Health, safety and environmental (HSE) risk — Oil and gas operations carry inherent HSE risks; failure to manage them could cause operational disruptions, environmental incidents, reputational damage and financial liabilities. Mitigated through HSE policies, training, emergency preparedness, safety audits and insurance cover on operated assets.
- Stakeholder and community relations risk — Operations sit in areas where relationships with local communities and landowners are essential; social or community issues, including land access pressure from increasing urbanisation around operating areas, may affect project execution and operational continuity.
- Climate change and energy-transition risk — The global shift towards lower-carbon energy, evolving climate-related regulations and rising stakeholder expectations on environmental performance may reshape the long-term operating environment for upstream oil and gas, and compliance may require additional operational and capital expenditure.
- Technology and cybersecurity risk — Growing reliance on digital technologies, operational systems and information infrastructure exposes the Company to cybersecurity threats, data security risks and potential business disruption.

themes.title: Oil & Gas - gas economy (CGD/LNG) + refining/upstream
themes.need: India's gas-economy push now collides with an outright policy reversal. ATGL grew volume 13% to 303 MMSCM and revenue 27% to INR 1,908cr, yet EBITDA FELL sequentially to INR 281cr (~14.7% margin, from INR 310cr) because the government withdrew the pooled-gas mechanism after the West Asia 'peace deal', pushing ATGL to ~15% spot volumes with Brent above $107/bbl; management also noted NWG price is 12% of the Indian crude basket, so a 62% domestic mix protects far less than it looks, and CNG station adds slowed to +5 from +25 in Q4 even as CNG demand grows ~30%. The same shock ran the other way for integrated refining: RELIANCE delivered O2C EBITDA of INR 17,000cr (+17%) THROUGH the Strait-of-Hormuz closure at 96-97% throughput while Asian peers ran 15-20% below capacity, with ethane+ROGC at ~70% of ethylene feed as distillate cracks blew out (gas oil $16 to $63, ATF $14 to $62). MGL/GUJGASLTD/IGL/IRMENERGY carry the same CGD margin squeeze; PETRONET/OIL/ONGC/IOC ride LNG-infra + domestic-gas; CHENNPETRO/MRPL ride GRM cracks; DEEPINDS/JINDRILL/SEAMECLTD on ONGC E&P capex; AEGISLOG/AEGISVOPAK add LPG/gas terminalling.
themes.driver: Whether the pooled/APM gas-allocation mechanism is restored (the single biggest CGD earnings variable); LNG spot price and Brent; GRM/distillate cracks; ONGC rig tenders & day-rates.
